title: Offline inference maintenance and hardware check - Aurum Pharma
summary: Discovery call focused on deploying Redwood Private in an air-gapped Aurum site. Key concerns: secure offline updates, vendor-signed images, hardware profile (A100 vs T4), limited outbound networking, maintenance windows, and auditability. Redwood AE + SE walked through potential architectures (private control plane vs fully air-gapped island), patch/update workflow (USB/signed bundle), and performance expectations. Agreement to run a perf benchmark on Aurum lab hardware and to share a detailed offline deployment checklist and signed-image process doc.
action_items: Alex (Redwood): Share offline deployment checklist + signed update example (due 2025-07-28)
Sam (Redwood SE): Prepare perf benchmark plan and test harness for Aurum A100 box (due 2025-07-30)
Jon (Aurum): Provide hardware inventory and BIOS/firmware constraints (due 2025-07-24)
Leena (Aurum): Share compliance requirements and SCAR/Risk template for air-gapped installs (due 2025-07-25)
next_steps: Run perf benchmark on Aurum dev rig (A100 x1) w/ 8k context; Redwood to coordinate remote start via offline instructions
Redwood to send signed-image update flow and verification checklist
Schedule pilot kickoff tentatively the week of 2025-08-04
Follow-up call to review benchmark results and discuss Dedicated reserved capacity vs private on-prem
meeting_header: Date: 2025-07-21 16:30 UTC | Duration: 57 min | Location: Zoom | Recording: enabled
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see we have Dr. Mira, Jon, Leena, and Kyle from Aurum. We'll do about 45-60 minutes. Sam and Diego from my side will cover technical details. Quick agenda: state of current infra, offline/update constraints, hardware profile, and next steps.

[00:28] Dr. Mira (Aurum): Hi, thanks. To be clear, our requirement is a fully offline inference environment in our R&D facility. No outbound internet, no agent that phones home, and updates must be cryptographically signed and applied manually.

[00:46] Sam (Redwood SE): Understood. When you say "no phone home" — do you allow a one-time outbound for registration through a bastion, or zero network at all?

[01:05] Jon (Aurum Infra): Zero network. The site is air-gapped for IP protection and regulatory audit reasons. Any updates go through our change control and are applied via removable media — usually USB or an internal tape/secure transfer.

[01:22] Alex: Okay. That maps to two common patterns: 1) Private deployment with a lightweight control plane inside your VPC (still needs some network connectivity between control plane and nodes) or 2) Fully isolated island where the control plane sits with you and Redwood provides signed artifacts and offline installers. Sounds like you want pattern two.

[01:41] Leena (Aurum): Yes, pattern two. Also need audit logs that we can ship to our SIEM; logs must be tamper-evident and we need to show who applied an update and the signing key.

[01:58] Sam: For signing, we can support images signed by Redwood and also allow you to re-sign with your HSM — we just need to agree on the verification step. We have an "offline bundle" workflow where we produce a tarball with a SHA256 and a detached signature, and you verify via OpenSSL/PKCS7, or you can provide a public key for verification.

[02:18] Jon: The verification tooling has to work on our side without pinging Redwood. Also, if there's a critical go-back, rollback must be straightforward. What's the rollback story?

[02:35] Diego (Redwood): Rollback: every node keeps the previous image snapshot and there's an atomic switch. We can provide scripts that perform verification and rollback locally. However, you should test it in your lab; we don't assume network reachability for orchestration.

[02:52] Kyle (Aurum): Quick question on hardware — our lab has an NVIDIA A100 40GB and a few older T4s. For initial pilot we'd likely use the A100 box. What perf can we expect for a 8k-context LLM and roughly how much RAM and NVMe do we need?

[03:12] Sam: On an A100 40GB, depending on model (open Llama family vs Llama 2 style weights) and quantization, you should expect sub-200ms token latency for streaming generation on 512-length prompts, but for 8k context it depends on KV cache memory. For a 70B model you need around 80GB peak memory unless you use 4-bit quantization and offload. NVMe for KV spillover is recommended if you must host very long contexts.

[03:38] Jon: We are not comfortable burning more than 1TB NVMe for the model and we'd prefer not to rely on host-swapping. What about model quantization recommendations?

[03:49] Sam: We typically recommend 8-bit or 4-bit quantized variants for on-prem in order to fit into 40GB. For your A100, compiled runtimes and kernel selection will matter a lot; we'll provide a quantization profile suggestion tailored to your model choice.

[04:05] Dr. Mira: What about throughput and batching? Our use case is not huge throughput but low latency for interactive research — 5 to 10 concurrent users at most.

[04:18] Diego: Given that, we won't need large reserved capacity. A single A100 should be fine for the pilot if you accept limited concurrency. We'll measure.

[04:31] Leena: Security point — how do we handle key management? We require keys stay in our KMS/HSM. Can Redwood sign images using our HSM?

[04:43] Alex: Yes, we can hand off the build artifact and also produce the signature you control. Two patterns: Redwood signs for convenience, but you also re-sign with your private key in the HSM prior to deploy. We can document the process so it meets your auditors.

[04:59] Jon: Patch cadence — how often do you expect customers to apply runtime patches? We have strict maintenance windows.

[05:10] Sam: We'll provide both regular update cadence and critical security patches as needed. For air-gapped installs, updates are manual. Our recommendation: monthly minor updates, quarterly major bundles, and immediate out-of-band patches if critical. All delivered as signed bundles.

[05:28] Dr. Mira: Can the instance still run telemetry locally (offline) so that we can collect performance metrics for our lab engineers? We want to generate usage and latency traces and keep the data in-house.

[05:42] Diego: Yes, observability agents can write logs locally to a mount point. We also support exporting tracing files that you can ingest into your SIEM. No telemetry leaves the site unless you explicitly export.

[05:56] Jon: About upgrade media: our process requires write-once media sealed and a second team member to sign-off. Do you provide checksums and signature verification that fit into that workflow?

[06:12] Alex: Yes. The bundle contains a checksum manifest and signatures, and we provide a verification script that prints the verification result and returns non-zero exit status on mismatch — designed for automated gating in your change-control process.

[06:28] Leena: We need to see evidence of SOC2 conformity and pen-test results. Also want to know if Redwood agents or components run as root in the host OS.

[06:40] Sam: We can share SOC2 report (redacted) under NDA. Regarding privileges: our runtime components can run in non-root containers; privileged operations (like x86 drivers) are isolated. We'll include a list of required capabilities.

[06:56] Dr. Mira: Any special kernel modules or driver versions required for the A100? We run a locked-down OS and updating drivers requires windows and approvals.

[07:10] Diego: For best perf we recommend driver NVRM >= 470 and CUDA 11.4+ for A100 families; however, we can also support older stacks with a performance tradeoff. We'll provide a compatibility matrix.

[07:26] Kyle: On the model side — do you offer model hosting of open-weight checkpoints or do we bring our own? We have proprietary research weights we'd rather keep inside the air-gapped zone.

[07:40] Alex: You can bring-your-own-model (BYOM). Redwood will run the inference runtime against your artifact locally; we do not need to take custody of your weights. For pilot we can also recommend community models to baseline performance.

[07:55] Jon: About licensing and support SLA — for private air-gapped we need on-call support and a documented escalation path. What are your support options?

[08:06] Alex: We have standard enterprise SLAs for Dedicated/Private customers. For air-gapped installs we offer an enterprise support add-on with 24x7 on-call and a named SE. Pricing and terms will be in the proposal.

[08:18] Leena: Can you walk through a hypothetical update: Redwood builds patch -> signs -> transfers to Aurum via secure courier -> Aurum verifies -> applies during maintenance window -> rollback tested. Any gotchas?

[08:34] Sam: The main gotcha is compatibility of driver/kernel and ensuring the verification tooling is run on the target host with correct keys. We'll include a preflight checklist: check kernel modules, NVMe health, available swap if using disk spill, signature verification, and free disk > X GB.

[08:54] Dr. Mira: About disk spill: we worry about NVMe wear if we use it for KV spill. Do you have recommendations for using NFS or remote storage inside the air-gapped network?

[09:06] Diego: NFS inside the air-gapped network is fine. If you have a high-end NVMe array you can configure it for write-intensity limits. We can suggest configuration. But for long contexts it's preferable to use memory-first strategies and quantization to avoid spill when possible.

[09:25] Kyle: Perf question — does Redwood support mixed precision and Tensor Cores usage automatically or do we have to recompile kernels?

[09:36] Sam: The runtime auto-selects kernels for mixed precision on supported GPUs and can take advantage of Tensor Cores. But in an air-gapped install we ship the runtime compiled for your target architecture and GPU drivers. If you block certain binaries, we can provide a source-level build pipeline for you to compile internally.

[09:57] Jon: If we compile internally, how do we prove the binary matches the artifact Redwood delivered? We need reproducible builds.

[10:08] Diego: Reproducible builds are hard but we can provide build manifests, Dockerfile config, and a deterministic build guide. For full reproducibility you'd run the build in your CI inside the air-gapped zone and produce your own signatures.

[10:28] Alex: Shifting to pilot scope: Sam, what minimal infra do we need to validate the use case?

[10:36] Sam: For the pilot: one A100 40GB node, 512GB NVMe (for model + spill), 256GB RAM, and a control VM for the orchestration/container host. We'll provide an image bundle and a verification tool. If you want to avoid NVMe we can test smaller context sizes initially.

[10:58] Dr. Mira: 256GB RAM is sizable; our lab doesn't have that much. Can we do with 128GB?

[11:05] Sam: Depends on model size. For smaller models and aggressive quantization 128GB will work. We'll tailor the benchmark to your model and quantify tradeoffs.

[11:16] Jon: On the bench tests — can Redwood provide a harness that we run offline which writes results to a CSV? We need to import into our internal perf dashboard.

[11:27] Diego: Yes, we'll provide a benchmark harness that produces token throughput, p50/p95 latency, memory, and disk IO stats in CSV/JSON. You can run it locally and share the results.

[11:38] Kyle: About the control plane — does it have to be present in the air-gapped network? Or can we run a minimal control plane externally and only copy artifacts?

[11:49] Sam: For fully offline you need a local control plane. The control plane coordinates container launches, health checks, KV cache management etc. We can minimize feature set for air-gapped: no metrics shipping, and a UI that runs on your internal network only.

[12:07] Leena: Also need RBAC integration with our IdP via SAML/SSO; can that be integrated locally?

[12:18] Alex: Yes, SAML can be configured against your internal IdP. It would be hosted locally; no external calls required. We document the SAML metadata exchange and the certs.

[12:30] Jon: Any PCI or HIPAA-specific notes? We are in pharma so clinical trial data is in scope for some projects.

[12:42] Sam: For PHI/clinical data we recommend full-disk encryption at rest and separation of data stores. Redwood Private supports encryption at rest with keys managed by your KMS. We'll include our data flow diagrams.

[12:56] Dr. Mira: Cost question — for a permanent private deployment how does pricing work? Is it reserved capacity or per-node license?

[13:07] Alex: For Private on-prem we do enterprise licensing (annual license + support) and optional reserved capacity pricing if you want Redwood-managed Dedicated pools. For air-gapped on-prem it's typically license + support + optional professional services for deployment. We'll put exact numbers in the proposal.

[13:25] Jon: Anything else we're missing?

[13:30] Leena: We want to see a sample SAAS-free architecture diagram and an incident response playbook that shows how you handle compromised nodes offline.

[13:42] Diego: We'll provide both a SAAS-free architecture diagram and an offline incident runbook; it will include steps for forensics, image re-signing, and wipe/reinstall.

[13:56] Alex: Quick recap and next steps: 1) Aurum to send hardware inventory and compliance checklist, 2) Redwood to send offline deployment checklist and signed-image example, 3) Redwood to prepare perf harness and schedule benchmark. Is that everyone?

[14:20] Dr. Mira: Yes. Can we lock a date for the bench? The week of Aug 4th is ideal.

[14:30] Alex: We'll tentatively schedule bench start 2025-08-05. Sam will own.

[14:36] Jon: One more thing — do you support TPM attestation for host verification? We use TPM-based boot attestation for critical nodes.

[14:45] Sam: We have a plan to integrate TPM-based attestation in the verification script; some details require access to your TPM tooling. We can support it as part of the pilot.

[14:58] Kyle: Small transcription note — is there a way to get the verification script in a package that our ops can inspect and sign? We don't want a binary blob.

[15:08] Diego: Absolutely. We'll deliver source-level scripts and a reproducible build guide.

[15:20] Leena: For legal, we'll need a statement that Redwood does not exfiltrate any customer weights or inference data in Private offline mode.

[15:30] Alex: We can include that language in the SOW and OS contract addendum.

[15:41] Dr. Mira: Thanks. Anything else?

[15:47] Alex: No, thank you. We'll follow up with the checklist and schedule.

[15:55] Jon: Thanks everyone.

[16:02] Speaker 6 (misc): [crosstalk] okay bye.

[16:12] -- End of recording (partial auto-transcript). Note: Transcript has occasional mis-hearings ("vp-see" for VPC, "kay-vee cache" for KV cache, "sock two" for SOC 2).
